source.description:
## What implementation this covers

Covers implementation issues xtrm-9xg2.1 and xtrm-9xg2.3 (canonical terminology + doctor/update/init flat-view runtime verification).

## Layer classification

Shell layer. This work validates user-facing command output and end-to-end runtime wiring across init/doctor/update surfaces.

## Strategy chosen

CLI integration tests and smoke tests:
- invoke real command constructors or CLI wrappers
- assert runtime-view output/messages use flat active path only
- verify failure text treats per-runtime tiers as legacy/invalid

## Test file structure

Extend existing shell-facing suites:
- `cli/test/doctor.test.ts`
- `cli/src/tests/update.test.ts`
- `cli/test/skills-runtime-sync.test.ts`
- add/adjust init or clean command assertions where message drift exists

## What to assert

- `xt doctor` JSON/text reports flat active view readiness only.
- `xt update` smoke output and JSON continue working with canonical flat path wiring.
- init/clean/user-facing strings no longer print `active/{claude,pi}`.
- Legacy per-runtime directory scenarios are handled as invalid drift, not expected layout.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Shell/integration coverage exercises doctor + update flat-layout behavior.
- [ ] Regression assertions catch stale `active/claude` / `active/pi` wording in command output.
- [ ] Tests reference xtrm-9xg2.1 and xtrm-9xg2.3.
- [ ] Coverage keeps canonical `.xtrm/hooks/` verification intact while updating active-view expectations.
source.title: Test: doctor/update/init flat active view shell smoke
